search_row.title: Fisher's infinitesimal model of quantitative inheritance
search_row.statement: Continuous traits determined by many Mendelian loci of small additive effect produce the observed correlations between relatives, so biometric and Mendelian inheritance are consistent.
search_row.math: Cov(z_i, z_j) = 2\Theta_{ij} V_A + \Delta_{ij} V_D; in the limit of M \to \infty loci the offspring trait given parents is Gaussian with mean (z_1+z_2)/2 and segregation variance V_0(1-\bar{F}), with error O(1/\sqrt{M}) (Barton, Etheridge and Veber 2017)

fields.dct:source: Ronald A. Fisher (1919) The Correlation between Relatives on the Supposition of Mendelian Inheritance
fields.delphi:proposedTest: Compare observed correlations between relatives of different degree in large pedigrees with 2*Theta*V_A + Delta*V_D, and check that the within-family segregation variance stays near V_0(1-F) under selection, as the limit theorem predicts.
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: many unlinked loci of small additive effect, random mating, environmental effects independent of genotype. Formal status: the covariance decomposition is proved; the infinitesimal limit, including under selection, is proved by Barton, Etheridge and Veber (2017). Large-effect loci and epistasis break the Gaussian limit.
